project: The Stock Market: From the Ground Up
scope: Original five-article targeted teaching sections and reproducible mathematical counterexamples; not full article republishing

sections.understand: SMA(3) means the arithmetic average of three eligible completed closes, in dollars per share. The window advances only when a new bar completes.
sections.recognize: Fictional 1-minute bars close at $10, $11 and $12; ($10+$11+$12)/3=$11. When a fourth bar finishes at $13, the eligible closes are $11,$12,$13 and the new SMA is $12.
sections.apply: Change the fourth completed close to $9 while leaving all other assumptions fixed. ($11+$12+$9)/3=$10.6667. Explain when this value becomes observable.
sections.commonMistake: Do not include a forming candle as a completed close, reuse the dropped $10 close, or call this SMA(9).
sections.limitations: Moving averages lag; a cross is not a guarantee of trend continuation, liquidity or profit.

sources.section: Tick vs. Minute Data; VWAP Formulas

sections.understand: Transaction VWAP is the sum of eligible trade price times shares divided by eligible shares, within a defined session and eligibility boundary.
sections.recognize: Two fictional trades: 100 shares at $10 and 300 at $12. The dollar-volume sum is $1,000+$3,600=$4,600; 400 eligible shares give $11.50/share.
sections.apply: Swap only the share counts to 300 at $10 and 100 at $12. The answer becomes $10.50, demonstrating why an unweighted mean of $11 is wrong.
sections.commonMistake: Never replace share weights with simple average of print prices or describe HLC3 bars as complete trade prints.
sections.limitations: VWAP is undefined for zero volume and depends on session, filtering and corrections; it is not an available fill guarantee.

sources.section: Tick vs. Minute Data; VWAP Formulas

sections.understand: Trade VWAP uses observed individual prints; HLC3-weighted bar VWAP is an OHLCV approximation. Bar aggregation discards information about prices and sizes of each print.
sections.recognize: Fictional prints 100×$20 and 400×$24 yield ($2,000+$9,600)/500=$23.20. A completed single bar H24/L20/C24/V500 produces proxy ($24+$20+$24)/3=$22.6667, $0.5333 lower.
sections.apply: Describe how another mix of trades could have the same OHLCV but different transaction VWAP. State what data would be necessary to reconstruct exact VWAP.
sections.commonMistake: Do not conflate quote-depth, executed prints, and an OHLCV aggregate. A bar approximation is not an exact trade reconstruction.
sections.limitations: Knowing a bar's H/L/C/V does not reveal the intra-bar volume distribution, and either derived number has no predictive guarantee.
sections.accessibleVisual: Printed trades: 100@$20 + 400@$24 => exact $23.20. Bar: H24 L20 C24 V500 => HLC3 proxy $22.67.

sources.section: Exponential Moving Average calculation and initialization

sections.understand: EMA(n) = alpha × completed close + (1−alpha) × prior EMA; alpha = 2/(n+1). A seed and warmup history must be declared to reproduce an early reading.
sections.recognize: Period=3 means alpha=0.5. Fictional closes 10,20,10,18, seeded with first close, give 10,15,12.5,15.25. An SMA(3) seed starts at bar 3 with 13.3333 and gives 15.6667 at bar 4.
sections.apply: Explain why different early EMA readings can arise from identical prices but different initialization. Do not assert that two vendors converge within a fixed number of bars without testing.
sections.commonMistake: Ignoring initialization, hidden prefetch and partial bars, or using alpha=2/3 rather than 2/4 for EMA(3).
sections.limitations: EMA is derived historical smoothing; early values and convergence depend on seed, precision, missing observations, adjustments and historical warmup.
sections.accessibleVisual: Close 10→20→10→18; first-close EMA 10→15→12.5→15.25; SMA-seeded EMA begins at bar 3: 13.3333→15.6667.

sources.section: Standard Deviation calculation divides squared deviations by n

sections.understand: A Bollinger-style band is a declared average plus or minus a specified number of standard deviations. State price source, period, center-line type, sigma denominator and multiplier.
sections.recognize: Fictional illustration using three completed closes 10,12,14, n=3 and k=2 (NOT the common 20-bar setting). Middle=12, squared deviations sum 8; population variance=8/3, sigma≈1.63299. Upper≈15.2660, lower≈8.7340.
sections.apply: Using sample denominator n−1=2 instead yields sigma=2 and bands 16 and 8. Explain why this is a convention change and not an identical calculation.
sections.commonMistake: Mixing sample and population standard deviation, applying 3-bar demonstration as 20-bar default, or interpreting a band touch as guaranteed reversal.
sections.limitations: Bands summarize prior dispersion, are sensitive to outliers and do not provide calibrated probabilities of future movement.
sections.accessibleVisual: Fictional closes 10, 12, 14; center 12; population-sigma lower 8.73 and upper 15.27; sample-sigma alternative lower 8 and upper 16.
